note: Consensus build philosophy from early FH6 guides. The fastest builds are usually NOT the highest-horsepower builds — grip and control first, power last.

upgrade_order.detail: Compound + front tire WIDTH. Widening front tires is now a valuable, PI-cheap grip fix before jumping to full compound.
Race brakes for braking stability and rotation.
Race springs/ARBs/dampers to unlock the tuning sliders.
Rarely wasted PI — improves braking, rotation, accel, and stability simultaneously.
AWD swap where traction-limited (see drivetrain rules). Decided by discipline.
Add power LAST, only up to what the chassis can deploy. Heavy engine swaps suit power tracks/sprints, hurt tight layouts.

drivetrain_rules.road_racing: AWD not mandatory; RWD can set faster clean laps but AWD launches harder, exits safer, survives contact. AWD favored online for consistency.
drivetrain_rules.early_meta_power_split: 30/70 front-to-rear is the early consensus AWD bias — launch traction with rear-biased rotation. NOTE: this is NOT a separate slider; it's the differential CENTER BALANCE set to ~70% rear. Don't look for a distinct 'power split' tuning option.

engine_swap_notes.heavy_v8_swap: 6.2L V8 swap is fast on power tracks/sprints but adds serious weight — reconsider on tight/touge layouts.
engine_swap_notes.principle: Conversions decide the car's ceiling. Get the conversion wrong and tuning only hides the damage.

build_principles: Keep most cars within 1-2 classes of stock; large class jumps create unstable builds unless the chassis is strong.
On tight circuits/touge the winner brakes cleanly, turns in hard, stays stable, and exits without wasting grip.
Spend PI on what the track rewards: top speed for highway zones, grip/brakes for technical routes.
